terms.notes: Taiwan decision note: for food-additive or nutritional-additive use, treat as not permitted unless the supplier provides a TFDA permit or official classification evidence. TFDA food additive standards use a positive-list approach: additives must match Appendix 1 scope/application/limits, and additives not listed cannot be used. Current Appendix I/II checks find calcium and magnesium glycerophosphate as separate entries, but not Potassium Glycerophosphate by exact name. This is not the same as a toxic/prohibited-substance blacklist ban; it is a positive-list non-listing. If the supplier claims this is an ordinary food ingredient rather than an additive, classification remains unresolved and must be supported by TFDA food ingredient query or official letter, product specification, Chinese name, exact salt identity, final food category, and use level. Do not approve import or label solely from the alias match.
